name: idsu
description: id(1) AND su(1), 2.11BSD's, on the credentials UFS 2.6 built.  THE POINT IS THE THIRD LINE: `su root' FROM nobody must be REFUSED, because upstream's rule is that only a member of group 0 in /etc/group may su to root, and nobody is not one.  That is the single assertion here that cannot pass by accident -- every other line would read identically on a machine with no permission model at all.  Around it: `id' as root reports uid=0(root) gid=0(wheel), which proves the passwd and group lookups resolve names rather than printing bare numbers; `su nobody' succeeds without a password because su skips the prompt for uid 0, which is the asymmetry wanted (root may become nobody, nobody may not become anyone); and `id' inside that shell reports uid=32767(nobody) gid=31(guest), which proves setuid AND setgid both took.  This is also the interactive half of what permtest does programmatically -- a way to BE a non-privileged user.

screen_contains: You do not have permission to su root
